= XTDB native Kafka adapter fork

This directory contains rust-rdkafka 0.38.0, paired with `../rdkafka-sys` 4.9.0+2.10.0 and its bundled librdkafka 2.10.0.
The upstream distributions and their license notices are retained.

`RetainedConsumerMessage` is a passive owner of a fetched native event and the consumer that produced it.
Its construction polls that consumer and moves the existing event into the owner without copying the payload.
The owner destroys the event before dropping its consumer reference.
The borrowed message view lasts for the owner's lifetime.
The event can retain a larger fetch or decompression buffer shared by native records.

`SslContextConfigurer` is a passive, shared configuration capability.
Its callback receives the linked OpenSSL `SSL_CTX` after native certificate and verification setup and before any connection starts.
The callback may install per-connection callbacks that borrow its immutable state.
The optional `replaces_default_trust` method suppresses automatic platform trust-store loading, CA path probing and OpenSSL default verify paths when the capability supplies replacement trust.
Its default is false.
Explicit native CA certificates, CRLs and client identities are still loaded before the callback.
The native configuration stores the selected flag, including across configuration duplication.
The optional `library_context` method supplies a borrowed OpenSSL 3 library context before native `SSL_CTX_new_ex` construction.
Its omitted implementation selects OpenSSL's default context.
The same retained capability owns that library context through the last native TLS object's destruction.
Explicit `ssl.providers` loads into that context, as do inline PEM keys and native PKCS12 stores.
PKCS12 decoding reuses an initialized context-bearing object, preserving the selected provider scope through integrity checking, decryption and private-key import.
`ClientConfig`, `NativeClientConfig` and every native configuration clone retain the capability.
A successfully created `NativeClient` takes ownership until `rd_kafka_destroy` returns.
The native pointer is destroyed before its retained callback capability.
Failure from `rd_kafka_new` leaves the caller's C configuration owned by Rust and releases it before the capability.
An already-created C client is under RAII ownership before log-queue setup can fail.
The temporary main-queue reference is also released.

The C API adds `rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_ctx_configure_cb` with a borrowed opaque pointer and a bounded error buffer.
Configuration duplication copies both callback and opaque fields.
`rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_ctx_libctx` adds the borrowed library-context pointer to that duplication contract.
Unsupported native builds reject a non-null library context.
The Rust wrapper supplies ownership for that borrowed pointer through an `Arc` and catches setup callback unwinding at the C boundary.
A native creation failure after TLS context setup destroys the context and loaded providers before librdkafka clears its copied configuration.
The fork requires its bundled C source; dynamic linking and external prebuilt librdkafka are rejected by the build script because those binaries lack this callback ABI.

The adapter uses OpenSSL's public context, certificate-selection and chain-checking APIs.
It does not inspect private C layouts or locate callback state through a global registry.
The consuming Kafka crate pins `openssl` 0.10.81 and `openssl-sys` 0.9.117, shared with the native dependency's OpenSSL linkage.

Primary references are https://github.com/fede1024/rust-rdkafka/tree/v0.38.0[rust-rdkafka 0.38.0], https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/tree/v2.10.0[librdkafka 2.10.0], https://docs.openssl.org/3.0/man3/SSL_CTX_set_cert_cb/[SSL_CTX_set_cert_cb] and https://docs.openssl.org/3.0/man3/SSL_check_chain/[SSL_check_chain].
Native ownership, default-trust replacement and handshake regression sources live in `../../crates/kafka/tests/native_tls_ownership.rs`, `../../crates/kafka/tests/native_tls_default_trust.rs` and `../../crates/kafka/tests/connect_registry_tls.rs`.
The fork and regression sources remain uncompiled and unexecuted in the source-only phase.

The native `sasl.scram.tokenauth` boolean defaults to false and is copied with the SASL configuration.
When enabled, the built-in SCRAM provider appends `tokenauth=true` to its client-first message.
The retained message without its GS2 header includes the extension when computing client proof and verifying the server signature.
This follows Kafka 4.4.0 `ScramLoginModule` and `ScramMessages.ClientFirstMessage`.
Regression sources in `../../crates/kafka/tests/native_scram.rs` cover native configuration duplication and invoke the bundled SCRAM message unit cases.

`SslContextConfigurer::material_source` optionally supplies a passive retained source of immutable native TLS file bytes.
`rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_material_cb` stores that callback and its owner across native configuration duplication.
The callback distinguishes borrowed bytes, a deferred OS read failure, and the unchanged filesystem loader.
An empty or unavailable snapshot never falls back to the filesystem.
The Rust wrapper catches material callback unwinding at the C boundary.
The bundled OpenSSL material API is required only when this optional source is supplied.

CA files, CRL files, certificate chains, private keys and native PKCS12 stores are decoded at their original loading sites.
CA and CRL files retain the common mixed-certificate/CRL PEM parser.
File certificates replace their chain, and file private keys use the selected library context and configured password callback.
Location and inline settings remain separate ordered inputs.
Native PKCS12 keeps its selected library context through decoding and password verification.
The source owner remains alive through destruction of native clients and their loaded keys.
The Rust adapter and qualification limits are documented in link:../../crates/kafka/src/client/material/README.adoc[native material ownership].

`SslMaterialSource::admit_context` optionally acquires one `Send + Sync` lease before each `rd_kafka_new` call.
Native configuration duplication does not share that lease: every resulting client requests its own admission.
A failed admission prevents native construction.
`SslMaterialLease::loaded` runs once after successful native creation and before the client is published, allowing temporary construction resources to be released.
The native pointer is under RAII ownership before this callback can unwind.
`NativeClient` destroys its pointer, including librdkafka's TLS context and provider cleanup, before dropping the retained lease.
The default method supplies no admission, preserving callers that have no material accounting policy.
This ownership seam does not itself bound OpenSSL allocations; the Kafka material source documents its explicit-file allowance and remaining qualification scope.

== Producer native byte account

A caller reserves capacity before creating a `NativeByteAccount` and passes the reservation to `NativeByteAccount::new`.
`ClientConfig::set_native_byte_account` shares that capacity among producers created from the configuration or its native duplicates.
Admin clients also use the native producer constructor.
A consumer configuration carrying an account fails at client creation.
The last safe owner blocks until all attached native clients and charged allocations have completed destruction, then releases the reservation on its Rust caller.
The producer's native main queue and the admin polling queue release their references before their owning client is destroyed.

The byte ceiling covers allocator-requested storage for incoming Kafka response frames on every broker connection and for requests submitted through the internal accounted Metadata entry point.
Each frame acquires its header and segment arena before reading the correlation ID.
After reading the declared size, it acquires additional storage before allocating the body, including any segment descriptor outside the original arena.
A late response, a partially read frame and overlapping responses keep their charges until their final native buffer references are released.
An admission failure during reception closes the connection and fails its outstanding requests with `RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__CRIT_SYS_RESOURCE` through the normal broker error path.
Callers should allow capacity for simultaneous responses, including connection setup.

The internal Metadata sender charges one contiguous request including its headers, client ID, encoded body and flexible tags.
It validates the client ID against the Kafka signed-short string length range before calculating the complete request size.
An invalid or oversized submission or an initial refusal returns a typed error before the C completion is installed.
Each transmission, retry and reply queue node has a separate charge until its own final free.
A node admission failure delivers its terminal error inline, including when another native owner releases capacity during error delivery.
The caller supplies a C completion that is valid on the submitting, serving, broker and teardown threads.
The account is a Monitor Object whose native release and client-detach operations signal the re-evaluable condition that both the live byte sum and attached-client count are zero.
The last Rust owner waits for native release before dropping the supplied reservation.

Ordinary Metadata responses admit their complete contiguous parsed arena before allocating it.
Checked sizing includes the aligned internal root, originating-broker name and existing wire-size estimate, with the rack-mapping factor when required.
Admission or native allocation denial returns `RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__CRIT_SYS_RESOURCE` and parse failure releases the arena charge after freeing its storage.
The root retains its account pointer and exact allocation charge through queue ownership and public C transfer.
`rd_kafka_metadata_destroy` frees the root before returning that charge.
Ordinary callback disposal, metadata-operation destruction and both admin projections use that final-release boundary.
DescribeTopics retains an unpublished description through diagnostic formatting, then cleans it up with the parsed arena if validation fails.
Both admin wrappers propagate the actual native parser/admission error even when it is separate from the response buffer's decode error.

Rust `Metadata` retains an account `Arc` independently of its originating client and destroys its native pointer before that guard.
Returned metadata can therefore outlive its producer without the producer's last account guard waiting on the caller's still-held result.
Direct C and C++ users must dispose their returned metadata owners before waiting for account destruction on the same caller.
Independent native metadata clones clear copied account ownership; their separate allocations remain unaccounted.
Mock and leader-discovery roots remain uncharged and initialize their ownership fields to zero.
The metadata cache, missing-topic lists, rack scratch, admin output copies, discovered brokers and other independent owners still require admission of their own.
The additive arena and admin source fixtures live in `../rdkafka-sys/librdkafka/src/rdkafka_metadata_account_test.h` and `../rdkafka-sys/librdkafka/src/rdkafka_metadata_admin_account_test.h`.
The Rust source fixtures include native regression dispatch and real MockCluster result lifetimes; neither has been executed in the source-only phase.

The account measures the listed native allocation requests.
The client, account monitor, existing queues, ordinary outbound requests, other protocol decoding, TLS and SASL machinery, allocator overhead and application-side result storage have separate ownership and sizing.
Regression sources live in `../../crates/kafka/tests/native_byte_account.rs` and `../rdkafka-sys/librdkafka/src/rdkafka_byte_account_test.h`.


`UPSTREAM.json` and `../rdkafka-sys/UPSTREAM.json` retain the original file hashes and registry archive identities.
The source archive SHA-256 values are `5f1856d72dbbbea0d2a5b2eaf6af7fb3847ef2746e883b11781446a51dbc85c0` for rust-rdkafka and `5230dca48bc354d718269f3e4353280e188b610f7af7e2fcf54b7a79d5802872` for rdkafka-sys.
The accounting changes retain each modified librdkafka file's upstream license header.
